03 / STATE GEOMETRY & INPUT MEMORY

Changing shape changes the accessible states.

QUANTUM METRIC eigenstate scan

Sensitivity to assembly twist

Twist 25–100° · metric in rad⁻²

Fubini–Study metric from squared eigenvector overlaps at θ ± 0.02°. The lowest exciton eigenstate is used; near-degenerate points are excluded. This is a separate static parameter scan, not Berry curvature or the mixed-state trajectory.

INPUT–OUTPUT EXPERIMENT two physical runs

How long do inputs remain different?

Press “Compare X / Y input encoding”

Two independent trajectories with identical geometry and environment. Plot: Frobenius distance ‖ρX − ρY‖ and signed excitation-population difference. This is a distinguishability diagnostic, not classification accuracy or proof of quantum advantage.

05 / RF & MAGNETIC PROTOCOL DESIGN

Specify the field before claiming the response.

Waveforms only · not coupled to P1H11

Helix axis and optical propagation: z. M3 transverse components: Bx = B₁ cos ωt, By = B₁ sin ωt; bias Bz = B₀. Two-cycle preview has its own ns time axis.

The missing microscopic connection

A waveform does not establish magnetic control of P1H11. The chemical drawing alone does not identify a paramagnetic spin, g-tensor, triplet population or relaxation time.

  • Needed: magnetic moments or susceptibility, relevant states and measured field response.
  • Then: add a dimensionally consistent −μ̂·B term, relaxation and experimental field geometry.
  • Separately: RF electric-dipole response, dielectric loss and heating.
  • Not inferred: magnetic “error healing”, condensation or topological protection.

Changing these RF controls intentionally does not change the optical trajectory. A negligible response must remain a possible scientific result.

06 / MATERIAL ANCHOR

P1H11, with its evidence attached.

(S)-phenyl-hexadecanoylamino-acetic acid methyl ester

Identity and stereochemical assignment supplied by the researcher. The drawing establishes connectivity; it is not a relaxed 3D conformation or measured aggregate structure. Nodes above represent effective chromophores, not all molecular atoms.

What the next release needs

  1. Verified 3D structures: monomer conformers and dimer / aggregate coordinate files.
  2. Electronic data: excitation energies, transition dipoles, transition densities and local-excitation / charge-transfer mixing.
  3. Structure ensemble: measured packing constraints, solvent, temperature and age.
  4. Optical validation: raw absorption, CD, emission and instrument conditions.
  5. Next solver: calibrated electrodynamics, then environment-driven structure evolution and a benchmarked computing task.
